ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, on the left side is the generator AC power supply, connected to the primary coil of the step-up transformer T1; the secondary coil of T1, after passing through the transmission-line resistance marked R above, is connected to the primary coil of the step-down transformer T2 on the right side; the right side of the secondary coil of T2 is connected only to a pure-resistance load R0. Therefore, when asking for “the input power of T2,” it corresponds only to the power at the input terminal of the step-down transformer itself, and does not include the loss on the transmission-line resistance R. Then reason: The problem gives R0=11 Ω, and the voltage across the electrical appliance is taken by effective value as U2=220 V. The load is a pure resistance, so the power consumed by the load is P load=U2^2/R0=220^2/11=4400 W. T2 is an ideal transformer, with no energy loss, so the input power of T2 equals the output power of the secondary coil, namely 4400 W.
